run_type: supplementary deep-search (user-requested incident response, not the scheduled routine)
trigger: User flagged the 2026-09-16 Japan Keytruda SC (Kiject) approval landing as a 'backfill' finding today as an incident, and asked for a deeper same-day sweep specifically to catch news that is fresh right now but at risk of only being fully covered by trade press a few days later (the same lag pattern that produced the Kiject miss: a regulator issues a batch/omnibus decision, and outlet coverage naming the specific SC/high-concentration angle trails by 1-3 days).

window.note: Same window as the scheduled 2026-09-21 run -- this is a deeper pass over the same window, not a new window.

queries_run.query: EMA CHMP opinion subcutaneous formulation September 2026
NMPA China approval subcutaneous biologic September 2026
CHMP positive opinion pembrolizumab subcutaneous perioperative bladder cancer September 2026 date
Merck.com Positive EU CHMP Opinion KEYTRUDA Padcev perioperative MIBC pembrolizumab SC press release date (verify candidate, primary source)

methodology_change_from_routine_run: Instead of the fixed 17-query company/technology-name matrix, this pass queried regulatory bodies and their recent decision batches directly (FDA, EMA/CHMP, Korea MFDS, China NMPA) plus company newsroom pages for tracked companies, on the theory that a near-miss like Kiject happens at the regulator-decision layer before trade press picks up the SC-specific angle. This is a slower, more expensive search pattern than the routine matrix and is not proposed as a wholesale replacement for it -- see recommendation below.

candidates.raw_title: EU CHMP positive opinion: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) + Padcev (enfortumab vedotin) perioperative MIBC, explicitly covering pembrolizumab SC (Keytruda SC/Qlex, ALT-B4-enabled)
candidates.gate_e: A CHMP positive opinion recommending EU approval of ALT-B4-enabled Keytruda SC in a new indication (perioperative MIBC) directly expands the addressable footprint of one of the two most commercially advanced hyaluronidase-based SC-conversion platforms this tracker benchmarks.

candidates.gate_e: Opdivo Qvantig is a major already-commercialized ENHANZE product (Halozyme's flagship licensed technology, already tracked) with zero deal rows in the tracker -- a pre-existing gap, not a fresh event.
candidates.reject_reason: Out of scope for this incident-response pass: this is a >1-year-old gap in ENHANZE coverage, not a same-day-freshness risk of the kind this deep search was launched to catch. Flagged to the user as a separate, pre-existing backfill opportunity rather than merged here, to keep this pass's diff scoped to the actual finding.

findings.event: EU CHMP positive opinion recommending Keytruda + Padcev perioperative MIBC, explicitly covering the ALT-B4-enabled Keytruda SC formulation
findings.summary: Published inside this run's search window (window opened 2026-09-18T09:02 KST; this is a same-day US press release, hours after window open) -- this is the genuinely fresh finding this deep-search pass was launched to catch before it could lag into a future backfill entry the way the 2026-09-16 Kiject item did.

recommendation: This confirms the incident's root cause is structural, not a one-off miss: the routine 17-query matrix is built around company/technology-name text search, which is exactly the layer where a regulator's own decision (CHMP opinion, PMDA/MHLW batch approval) precedes dedicated SC-angle trade-press coverage by 1-3 days. A durable fix is to add a standing regulatory-calendar check to the routine matrix -- e.g. an EMA CHMP meeting-highlights check and a Japan MHLW/PMDA batch-approval check -- for the tracked hyaluronidase-enabled products (Keytruda SC, Opdivo SC/Qvantig, LEQEMBI SC) each run, rather than relying on company-name text search to surface a regulatory body's own announcement. This is a SKILL.md change (adding to the Tier-3/Tier-4 query set), not a data change, and is flagged to the user for a decision rather than made unilaterally in this run.
